Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (infrastructure) and Marissa (compliance) — they can provide the technical and contractual detail.

High level for the customer:
- Deletions are initially represented as tombstone markers; physical expunge happens after the retention/TTL expires and an expunge cycle runs.
- Within the same primary region we expect tombstone to be quiesced and eligible for expunge within 24–48 hours for normal workloads. Cross-region replication means the tombstone is replicated quickly (seconds–minutes), but the expunge window is aligned with regional retention sweeps and can take longer to complete if replicas are still keeping copies for DR.
- Immutable snapshots and cold offsite archives are treated as separate retention classes — they are not auto-expunged by the standard expunge sweep until their snapshot TTL elapses or a manual purge is initiated.

I'll attach a short diagram and a retention matrix; Rishi — can you confirm the typical worst-case timelines and note any exceptions (e.g., HSM/KMS key lifecycle, legal hold overrides)?

Priya / team —

Adding the technical details Jake requested. I'll keep this tight so it can be pasted into customer-facing language.

1) Deletion model and tombstones- Primary delete: when an object or dataset is deleted via API or console an internal tombstone marker is written to metadata; that tombstone is replicated to peer replicas (same region and cross-region async replication). Replication of the tombstone is fast (typ. < 60s) but does not by itself remove physical blocks.
2) Expunge / garbage collection- Expunge is performed by periodic garbage collection sweeps that look for tombstones older than the dataset's retention threshold (configurable per-customer, defaults described below). The expunge job will remove blocks and free space; this can be completed in the primary region within 24–72 hours after the tombstone becomes expunge-eligible under normal load. Cross-region expunge timing depends on regional sweep schedules (we stagger sweeps to avoid peak load) and on replication lag — typical cross-region full expunge completion is 48–168 hours from tombstone creation in worst-case operational conditions.
3) Retention classes and snapshots- Snapshots that are created as immutable (write-once) are excluded from expunge until the snapshot TTL expires or an authorized manual purge is requested. Offsite cold archives follow a separate lifecycle (archival tier) and require a manual purge request; we can show these as exceptions in the SLA.
4) Key management and encrypted backups- If a customer's KMS/HSM key is scheduled for destruction, ciphertext remains unreadable but physical copies could remain until expunge runs. KMS key destruction is a separate irreversible operation; we recommend customers coordinate key retirements with data expunge windows if they require cryptographic erasure guarantees.
5) Legal hold / litigation- Legal hold overrides standard retention/expunge. When a legal hold is in place we mark those datasets as non-expungeable until the hold is lifted and the TTL passes. Lifting the hold resumes normal tombstone/expunge flow.

Exceptions & notes-
- Snapshot immutability and manual offsite archives are common reasons deletion appears to 'persist' longer; we should call these out explicitly.
- Backup copies retained by our CDN or partner cold-storage vendors may have different retention/expunge windows — we can include partner SLAs if needed.

Suggested customer-facing summary (one paragraph):
"When you delete data, Redwood marks it for deletion immediately and replicates that deletion across replicas within minutes. Physical removal of backup data occurs after retention thresholds are met and expunge cycles run — typically within 1–3 days in the primary region and up to a week for cross-region replicas in worst-case conditions. Immutable snapshots or offsite archives are excluded from normal expunge flows and require separate purge actions or TTL expiration. Legal holds and key-retirement processes can extend these timelines; we recommend coordinating those events with your account team."

I'll attach the diagram (backup-delete-flow-diagram.pdf) and the retention matrix (retention-policy-matrix.xlsx) for the legal/compliance team. If we want to offer a shorter cross-region expunge SLA (e.g., guaranteed 72h expunge) we should surface this as an enterprise addendum (Reserved capacity + operational controls).

-Rishi
